description: We are PlasmaX, a team passionate about space exploration, science, and technology. We are developing a lunar landing site navigator, an innovative platform using real NASA data, 3D lunar terrain, and scientific simulations. We value creativity, teamwork, and innovation. We welcome talented members skilled in Python, React, astronomy, physics, AI, data science, 3D design, UI/UX, and research, as well as motivated learners eager to contribute!
summary:
We developed a 3D simulation and software to plan help mission planners, engineers, and scientists plan for lunar south pole missions precisely. Our application is a combination of accurate, precise calculation using NASA data and an interactive, engaging interference.

In our simulation there is:
- 3D simulation of lunar typography using NASA LOLA data
- Input from user about specific time, coordinates, and ability to choose any place on the moon, with our software directly calculating the latitude and longitude.
- Time and position metric comparisions.
- Output metrics for specific time and location. (e.g: sunlight angle, Earth connection, etc...)
- Timeline to interactively choose any time of your choice to calculate and plan for.


We believe that PlasmaX is the start of change for our view to precise software from being accurate but complex to being accurate and interactive.
details:
Project Overview & Concept

PlasmaX is an advanced 3D lunar landing site navigator engineered specifically for NASA missions targeting the lunar south pole. Traditional mission planning software is often overly complex, sluggish, or disconnected from real-time environmental variables. PlasmaX bridges this gap by combining highly accurate, authentic NASA planetary datasets with an interactive, lightning-fast web interface designed for mission planners, engineers, and scientists.

How It Works & Key Features

  • 3D Lunar Topography & Simulation: Powered by authentic NASA LRO LOLA (Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter Lunar Orbiter Laser Altimeter) elevation data and LROC global mosaics, PlasmaX renders a fully interactive 3D Moon globe.
  • Dynamic Timeline Scrubbing: Features a real-time synodic timeline slider allowing users to scrub through a 29.53-day lunar cycle to track changing shadows, sun angles, and illumination patterns.
  • Precise Coordinate & Metric Calculators: Users can select any point on the lunar surface (e.g: Shackleton Crater Rim) to automatically compute exact latitude/longitude coordinates.
  • Comprehensive Output Telemetry: Instantly calculates critical landing constraints for any selected time and location, including Sun Elevation Angle, Earth Line-of-Sight (DSN communication margins), and Surface Slope Safety Gradients.

Technology Stack

  • Structure: HTML
  • Coding / Software: JavaScript (JS), Node.js (for backend environment and package management), and JSON (for structured data and coordinate mapping)
  • 3D Integration / Framework: Three.js (for rendering interactive 3D lunar topography and lighting models)
  • Framework / Build Tool: Vite (for fast frontend development and asset bundling)

Intended Impact & Significance

PlasmaX redefines mission planning software by proving that high-precision scientific accuracy doesn't have to come at the cost of usability. By giving engineers rapid visual feedback on lighting, communication blockages, and terrain hazards, PlasmaX prevents costly mission anomalies (such as shadow blackouts or terrain tipping) and helps secure a sustainable human footprint on the Moon.
